Synopsis:
Player finds a talking mirror that seems to be guarding a door to its old master's secret room. It doesn't recognise you as its master, so it challenges you with three questions to see if you're  friend or foe. If you get the questions wrong, it activates a trap to try and kill you. The mirror hasn't been used in a long time - its master died years ago. The mirror speaks in a cracked, broken voice.

Cluster Contexts:
- FOR_ThayanCellar_MagicMirror.json: You stand before an ornate, sentient mirror set into a door that protects its late master's secret room; the mirror acts as a ward and judge, speaking in a cracked, stuttering voice and staring with glassy eyes. Its master, Ilyn Toth, has been dead for years, so the mirror no longer recognizes new faces and tests anyone who claims alliance by asking three questions to prove friend or foe. One of the questions references Szass Tam — knowledge of the Red Wizards and Thay is therefore useful — and correct answers will grant you passage while failures trigger a lethal trap. The mirror’s memory and upkeep are old and faltering, so it can be tricked, argued with, or angered by a brash response.
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_FatherCarrion.json: Dialog with Mystic Carrion, a mummy lord hiding in the Lower City. Players who carry the Necromancy of Thay (unread) have the chance to take part in a seance where they can learn how the book can be opened. Players can also take on a quest from Carrion, to bring back his runaway zombie beggar Thrumbo (potentially in exchange for the torch of revocation, intended to help Oskar).Various conclusions are available for the quest to help Mystic Carrion - if the player succeeds in bringing himThrumbo's torso, he will reward them with a Torch of revocation which can be used to cure Oskar's possession (Oskar's Beloved). If you refuse him, he will attack you, and keep returnign from the dead until you destroy his canopic jar (hidden inside Thrumbo)
- UND_DuergarCamp_Checkpoint.json: After you sail to the other side of the Darklake, two duergar greet you. If Greymon is with you, he confirms you are a True Soul - as long as you don't mention the boots. Otherwise, the player is revealed as a True Soul through a mindmeld-type moment.there. Morghal tells you that another True Soul, Nere, is trapped above, then asks for a bribe to let you in.

context: You stand before an ornate, sentient mirror set into the door of Ilyn Toth’s secret room; its master died years ago, so the mirror no longer recognizes new faces and acts as a ward and judge. In a cracked, stuttering voice it demands that anyone claiming alliance prove it by answering three questions — one question explicitly tests knowledge of Szass Tam and the Red Wizards. If you answer correctly the mirror will grant passage; if you fail it will trigger a lethal trap. The mirror’s memory and upkeep are faltering, so it can be tricked, argued with, or provoked by brash or evasive responses.
